A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEAL and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched across the supplementary-material reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original SEAL evaluations on LVBench, MovieChat-1K, and Ego4D-NLQ, together with ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds empirical efficiency measurements, relevance-encoder ablations, and a 7B LVBench comparison.

M1.justification: Semantic decomposition, relevance/diversity selection, streaming updates, and prediction heads remain the same. The newly specified object-crop expansion and Ego4D token selection are implementation disclosures; the PDFs do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use LVBench, MovieChat-1K, and Ego4D-NLQ with the same task coverage, including partial-video scenarios. The added encoder, model-size, and efficiency experiments introduce no new dataset, domain, or task requirements.

E2.justification: New Table 11 compares SEAL at 7B against MovieChat, TimeChat, and the cited MA-LMM work, printed as MA-LLM, on LVBench. These extend the reported LVBench comparisons; comparator membership in the retained Tables 1-3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a separate 7B LVBench evaluation, relevance-encoder variants, and token-budget sweeps measuring inference FPS including all processing from raw frames. The original benchmark protocols, training settings, and main model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a relevance-encoder ablation using BLIP, CLIP, and BLIP2 (Table 10), an accuracy-efficiency analysis (Figure 4), and selected-token composition statistics (Appendix B). Existing token-type, tracker, streaming, partial-observation, alpha-sensitivity, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the qualitative discussion of high summarization variance; the new experiments introduce no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1-9 are retained. New Table 10 reports overall accuracies of 45.9%, 42.9%, and 40.5% for BLIP2, CLIP, and BLIP; Table 11 reports 36.6% for SEAL at 7B versus 22.5%, 22.3%, and 24.5% for its comparators. Figure 4 adds accuracy-speed findings, and Appendix B adds token proportions. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces max with argmax and excludes self-pairs from the diversity sum. These clarify the existing fixed-size subset optimization: removing cosine self-similarities removes only a constant. No substantive assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified semantic tokens, relevance/diversity attention, global and streaming processing, and strong performance across the three benchmarks. The added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 attributes the encoder-ablation gains to better relevance estimates and explains using only scene/action tokens for Ego4D as preserving temporal consistency. Existing limitations concerning solver memory, end-to-end training, causal reasoning, and stylized visual content remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies expanding object bounding boxes by 2x for contextual features and explicitly states that Ego4D uses only scene and action tokens. Existing extraction parameters, token budgets, and LLM prompts are retained. These disclosures do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: The introduction adds the Protege temporal-grounding citation, reference 39 in v3. The related-work narrative and unified-representation positioning remain largely unchanged; the methods newly compared in Table 11 were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites portions of the abstract and introduction, condenses ablation and conclusion prose, updates author information, and adds acknowledgements. Supplementary headings are revised, while the main section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the accuracy-FPS plot and Tables 10-11, relocates Table 4 and several appendix displays, and reorders the Human row in Table 9. Existing diagrams, qualitative examples, and plots are retained with resizing, caption edits, and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens support for efficiency through accuracy-FPS measurements and adds useful 7B comparisons and relevance-encoder ablations. The implementation disclosures also improve transparency. These are focused gains over v1, with the original results and limitations retained; the new timing evidence remains incompletely reproducible because hardware details are unspecified.
